body:
**Claiming this and taking it to a fix** — I filed it from the application side; the maintainer has asked for it solved rather than worked around, because it blocks a Chinese-language first release.

- Session: `session_01SqkTcrxUFci7nqXdbBSe2p`
- Branch: `claude/group-company-task-tracking-astg44` (this session's designated branch, restarted from `origin/main`; it carried no commits and had never been pushed)

### Scoping done before dispatch, so the shape is on the record

Reading the code changes two things about how big this is.

**The dispatch table is the single seam, and it already knows that.** `METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS` in `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` is the one table, and `TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES` is *derived* from it rather than restated — with a comment saying that is deliberate so "adding a translator here reaches the REST boundary with nothing else to remember (#3786)". So surface 3 (datasets) is a `translateDataset` plus one table entry plus a schema group, and the REST surface follows for free.

**Surface 2 is much smaller than the issue implies.** I wrote that the rule message is emitted verbatim with nowhere to look up a translation. The *lookup mechanism* is in fact already there: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:2342` holds `private i18nService?: { t? }`, and `:5603` documents it as "the i18n service used to localize **write-path validation messages** and field-label localization (#3957)". Built-in field-catalog messages already flow through it. What is missing is only a **key shape for an author-written rule** — not a channel to resolve one. That is a correction to my own issue body worth having before anyone starts.

Surface 1 (`bulkActionDefs`) stays as described: an extension inside `translateView`, since a bulk-action def is part of the view document.

One PR, three commits, one per surface — they share `translation.zod.ts` and splitting them across PRs would just serialise a conflict.

### Acceptance is measurable from outside

`objectstack-ai/duly` carries all three as **declared, reasoned exemptions** in its i18n coverage walk (`src/translations/authored-text.ts`), and its gate fails when an exemption stops matching. So when this lands, that app's gate goes red on the three stale exemptions — which is the signal the fix is real, not a claim about it. The screenshots in this issue are from that app and can be re-taken against the fix.

**Dev seat claim** — picking this up from the PM dispatch above; same session, so this is a continuation of that claim, not a competing one.

- Session: `session_01SqkTcrxUFci7nqXdbBSe2p`
- Branch: `claude/group-company-task-tracking-astg44` (already checked out in the shared primary checkout, so this seat works from a **detached** worktree at `origin/main` and pushes with an explicit refspec — `git push -u origin HEAD:claude/group-company-task-tracking-astg44`. The shared checkout's HEAD is not touched.)
- Base: `origin/main` @ `4fac7a02`

Re-read the comment thread before starting: the only prior claim is the PM's, under this same session ID. No competing claim.

Plan follows the scoping comment: one PR, three commits — `bulkActionDefs` inside `translateView`, an `_validations.RULE.message` key shape resolved through the **existing** `i18nService` channel in objectql (no second i18n path), and `translateDataset` registered in `METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS` so the derived `TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES` carries it to the REST boundary. Each surface gets a test that is red without the fix.

Triage (R+89, triage seat, session `session_019kDRpB7D2XzVzkaLp57T5D`): **state machine brought in line with the live thread — `pm:dispatched`** · `priority:p1` · `domain:spec` · type **Feature**. ⛔ This is not a dispatch by the triage seat; the card is already claimed (assignee `os-warren`, claim + dev-seat continuation under `session_01SqkTcrxUFci7nqXdbBSe2p`, branch `claude/group-company-task-tracking-astg44`) and the claim records the maintainer's own direction ("the maintainer has asked for it solved rather than worked around, because it blocks a Chinese-language first release") — the maintainer direct-route channel. A claimed card carrying no `pm:*` label is invisible to every lane and patrol view, which is the only thing corrected here.

**Routing note for the landing:** all three surfaces land in `packages/spec` (`translation.zod.ts`, `i18n-resolver.ts`'s `METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS`), and each adds a translation key shape to a published schema ⇒ **Clause-②: yes** — the delivered PR goes through the contract-review tier before it is enqueued (`needs:contract-review` on the PR when it opens; the spec seat or an at-tier reviewer clears it). The `_validations.RULE.message` half rides the **existing** `i18nService` channel in objectql, per the claim's own correction — ⛔ no second i18n path.

Liveness: datasets seeded live and DRILLED with its reader in the same change; two stale ledger sentences corrected alongside (the translation header still called validationMessages 'the one dead group' a major version after #4667 removed it, and validation.message's note still named it as the override route).",

TWO GATES WERE RED FIRST and are recorded rather than hidden: `check:doc-authoring` caught two `#NNNN` citations I had written into customer-facing tombstone text (fixed in commit 4, which also adds the negative pin the gate's own remedy asks for), and five spec dist-reading gates refused on a stale dist after the reverse-verification restores moved src mtimes (rebuild, then green). EXTERNAL ACCEPTANCE: objectstack-ai/duly at dd3c619, its i18n gate run twice — baseline on published 17.2.0 = 29 passed; with node_modules/@objectstack/spec repointed at this branch's build (untracked symlink, trap-restored and verified back to ../.pnpm/@objectstack+spec@17.2.0/..., duly's tree left clean) = 1 failed / 28 passed, the failure being 'pins the metadata types the PLATFORM says are translatable' with 4 elements where 3 were expected. On long-term soundness: object-scoped addressing with a reader in the same change is strictly the sound version of what was retired, and it adds no consumer-side tolerance. On making AI-written metadata hard to get wrong: the key face is one key, every neighbouring spelling that would translate nothing is refused with guidance naming the right home, and the two tombstones now route authors to a live key instead of a dead end — which is a net reduction in ways to get this wrong. On startup scope discipline: this is not a capability expansion, it is closing a hole in a shipped capability with zero new authoring surface beyond one optional string. The only axis pulling toward B is the paper trail, and that is cheap to add later without touching this code. ⛔ Do NOT read this as a request to hold the PR: it is a ratification question, and C is listed only for completeness."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope_findings": [
    "filed as #14376: i18n-extract scaffolds none of the three new key families, so `os i18n extract` will not offer them and `check:i18n-coverage` cannot see them — third time this exact follow-up has been needed (#11485, #13109), so the card also asks whether the fix should be structural rather than a fourth manual walk. Blocked-by #14253; kept out because it moves nine generated bundles and the coverage baseline.",
    "filed as #14377: the published skill `skills/objectstack-i18n` teaches that validation messages are not a translation group — false once this lands. `skills/**` is a governed surface, so it may not ride a mixed diff; the card carries the net-line-budget warning and flags a collision with the open DIET card #14315 on the same file.",
    "filed as #14378 (label `finding`): `rest-server.ts:2963` restates the translatable-type set by hand inside `translateMetaItem`, and this change makes that parenthetical short by one. Left alone deliberately — a one-word comment edit is not worth the conflict risk in that file. The card also records that the similar sentence in `conversions/registry.ts:3039` should be LEFT as it is, being the historical rationale for a 17.0.0 retirement."
  ]
